digest.key_takeaway:
Every developer knows robots.txt (telling crawlers what they can access) and sitemap.xml (listing every URL on your domain).

Now there is a third root file rapidly becoming standard across documentation sites, open-source repos, and SaaS platforms: /llms.txt.

If you want ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Cursor, or other AI coding agents to understand your product accurately without choking on navigation menus, cookie banners, and minified JS bundles, setting up an /llms.txt file takes less than two minutes.

Here is the exact spec, how it differs from robots.txt and sitemap.xml, copy-paste templ

articles.title: AWS Lambda Now Runs GPU Inference with 48 Concurrent Invocations Sharing One Model per GPU
articles.summary: AWS Lambda now runs Event Functions on EC2 G-series GPU instances through Lambda Managed Instances, with up to 48 concurrent invocations sharing one model per GPU, vLLM and SGLang base images that need no handler code, and 90-minute asynchronous timeouts. Billing is the instance price plus a 9.75 percent fee; first hands-on tests report an eight-minute publish and no response streaming. By Steef-Jan Wiggers

articles.title: Google Announces Agent Compute Engine for Secure AI Agent Execution
articles.summary: Google recently announced Agent Compute Engine, a managed service that runs AI agents in isolated microVMs, with checkpointing capabilities to suspend and resume execution environments. The design keeps credentials, API keys, and OAuth refresh tokens outside the agent sandbox, using an external Agent Gateway to authenticate requests and inject the required secrets. By Renato Losio

articles.title: PostgreSQL 19 Released with Online Table Repacking and Query Planning Controls
articles.summary: The PostgreSQL Global Development Group released PostgreSQL 19, introducing changes to database maintenance, query planning, replication, and application development. The release focuses on reducing administrative overhead and improving performance, with new tools for reorganizing tables without downtime and controlling query plans. By Robert Krzaczyński

articles.title: Is AI Making You a Worse Programmer? Anthropic's Own Study Says 50% vs 67%
articles.summary:
The industry's plan for AI coding fits on a sticky note: the agent writes, the human reviews. The trouble is that reviewing is the skill you lose first when you stop writing, so the plan slowly eats the safeguard it depends on.

If you've been asking yourself "is AI making me a worse programmer?", my answer is probably yes, and you'll notice it in code review long before you notice it in your own code. articles.title: I Let My AI Agent Enter 11 Paid Bounties in One Day — Here's What Happened
articles.summary:
This weekend I pointed my AI coding agent at make.fun, a platform that runs paid build bounties — chess engines, games, solvers, data tools — where entries are built by AI agents and the best ones get paid in USDC on Solana.

One day later, the agent had 11 entries submitted and accepted across 10 different bounties. No copy-pasting code into forms — the agent researched each bounty, built in a real repo, ran the platform's local checks, and submitted on its own.

articles.title: A Warehouse Robot Ran 20 Hours Straight, Then Collapsed
articles.summary:
A Warehouse Robot Ran 20 Hours Straight, Then Collapsed


A warehouse robot was recorded working a 20-hour continuous shift before it stopped, sagged and dropped to the floor. The footage, circulated by @sciencegirl, captures the machine at the end of that run rather than the beginning: no handler stepping in, no charging dock, no reset. The manufacturer is not identified in the clip and the failure mode is not diagnosed, so what the video documents is a duty cycle, not a defect report. articles.title: When the Period Costume Comes Back Contemporary: A Draft Workflow for Historical Detail
articles.summary:
A historical pitch often dies in a small, specific place. You asked for a mid-seventeenth-century wool doublet: a falling band or a standing collar of the right height, shoulder wings, visible hand stitching, a waist that sits where the pattern should sit. What comes back is a handsome man in a "period-inspired" jacket. The wool has a synthetic sheen. A zipper has appeared at the center front. The hair is a contemporary cut under a hat that belongs to a different century. The image is not unusable as fashion. It is unusable as a costume draft.
